bounded-context.name: Orders
bounded-context.purpose: The transactional spine of the store. Owns the checkout flow from cart to placed order, the LineItem value type, and the canonical OrderPlaced event every downstream consumes.
bounded-context.narrative:
Checkout starts when a customer freezes their at . The service reserves stock through the anticorruption layer, which translates Orders' view into terms so neither context has to learn the other's vocabulary. Once every line reserves, Orders emits ; opens an from that event, and schedules a shipment in parallel.
Money flows through the kernel value, so a price captured at add-to-cart time survives the trip to Billing without re-denominating. The whole flow respects : the order total is the sum of its line items, computed at place-order and never silently mutated downstream.

term.name: `Cart`
term.definition: A mutable pre-checkout container for a customer's intended purchase. Lives for at most 30 days from last update; abandoned carts are not orders and do not appear in any report.
term.identity-rule: Stable by `cartId`. A Cart survives session boundaries (signed-in customers) but a fresh anonymous session begins a new Cart.

term.name: `LineItem`
term.definition: A single row in a Cart or Order: `{sku, quantity, unitPriceAtAdd}`. The price is captured at add-to-cart time, not at checkout — a price change between add and checkout does not silently reprice the customer's basket.
term.equality: Two LineItems are equal iff their `sku`, `quantity`, *and* `unitPriceAtAdd` match. Adding the same SKU twice produces one line with `quantity += 1`, not two lines — see .

term.name: `Order`
term.definition: An immutable record of a placed order. The transition `Cart → Order` is one-way: once placed, line items, prices, and shipping address are frozen. Refunds and cancellations live on , not by mutating the Order.
term.identity-rule: Stable by `orderId` (UUID v7, monotonically increasing — used as the natural sort key for "most recent orders" reads).

term.name: `placeOrder`
term.definition: The checkout operation. Atomically: reserves stock through the seam, freezes the Cart's line items, computes the total, persists the Order, emits . Returns the new Order or a typed rejection (`OutOfStock`, `PriceChanged`, `InvalidPayment`).
term.returns: `Result<Order, PlaceOrderRejection>`. Rejections are enumerated; surprises are bugs.

term.name: `OrderPlaced`
term.definition: The published event marking the Cart-to-Order transition. The single fanout point downstreams use to start their own work — billing opens an invoice, inventory commits the reservation, shipping schedules a shipment.
term.emitted-when: succeeds and the Order has been persisted. Never emitted speculatively.
term.payload: `{ orderId, customerId, lineItems: SKU[], totalMinor, currency, placedAt }`. Anything else (shipping address, payment method) is fetched by the consumer from the Orders read API.

invariant.name: Order total equals sum of line totals
invariant.statement: For every Order, `total = Σ(lineItem.quantity × lineItem.unitPriceAtAdd) + shippingMinor + taxMinor`. The equality holds in minor-unit integers exactly — no rounding drift.
invariant.rationale: The Order total is what the customer pays and what every downstream report sums. A drift between total and line sum is the kind of bug that hides for months in dashboards before someone audits a single Order by hand. Re-deriving and asserting at place time is cheap insurance.

invariant.name: Cart never has two line items with the same SKU
invariant.statement: Adding the same to a Cart twice produces one LineItem with `quantity += 1`, not two LineItems. A Cart with duplicate SKUs is a bug.
invariant.rationale: Duplicate SKU lines break the line-sum invariant above (rounding-different unitPriceAtAdd values create rows that look identical but don't sum) and confuse the checkout UI (which collapses on display anyway, hiding the bug). Catching this at the add-to-cart call site is cheaper than after.

aggregate.name: Order aggregate
aggregate.rationale: The Order and its LineItems are persisted together or not at all. Concurrent modifications to the same Order are rejected with an optimistic-concurrency error rather than merged. The aggregate boundary is what makes "order-placed event is never out of sync with the persisted order" a tractable invariant.

seam.name: Orders ↔ Inventory
seam.description: Orders never thinks in `StockItem` or `Reservation` — those are Inventory's atoms. At checkout, Orders calls Inventory through an ACL that translates `(sku, quantity)` requests into Inventory's Reservation model and translates the response back into Orders' `LineItemReserved` / `LineItemOutOfStock` outcomes. The ACL lives in `src/orders/inventoryClient.ts`.
seam.rationale: Inventory's model is rich (multi-warehouse stock pools, backorder flags, reservation expiry windows) but irrelevant to Orders' checkout step. Letting that vocabulary bleed into Orders would make every Orders test depend on Inventory's full state machine. The ACL lets Inventory evolve its model freely; only the ACL contract needs to keep up.

boundary-rule.rule: Orders never writes to Inventory's data store. Reservations are created and released only through the Inventory API exposed via the ACL above.
boundary-rule.rationale: Direct writes from Orders would let two contexts race on the same stock row and would scatter reservation logic across both codebases. Routing all stock changes through Inventory is what makes the reservation-expires invariant in tractable.
